card.name: Words just before patient-population terms
card.fires_on: The word "in" or "General"/"general" where the next words likely name a patient group or field, such as adult patients, patients over age 24, or General Medicine.

modes.label: "in" before a patient group
modes.description: The word "in" after a drug or condition, leading into a population such as adult patients or subjects over a certain age.
modes.example: These studies did not show an increase in the risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior with antidepressant use<< in>> patients over age 24; there

modes.description: "General" in a medical division title, just before "Medicine".

modes.label: Start of "generalizability"
modes.description: The start of the word generalizability, split after "general", in discussion of how far study results apply.

card.writes: It seems to push toward clinician and clinical-setting words such as dr and clinical, and away from other continuations.
card.plain: It fires on small words that lead into who a finding applies to, or into a medical specialty name.
